B"H

# Phase 3 — Thirty Additional Hardening Improvements

The Awtsmoos renews the interface and contract before every request can claim stability;
Awtsmoos.com must make universality survive evolution, latency, offline states, mobile constraints, and operational reality.

1. Resource envelopes need explicit envelope-version metadata independent of domain type version.
2. Clients need forward-compatible unknown-field handling and must never reject an envelope merely because a new optional capability appears.
3. Type registry responses need cache validators and revision IDs so clients can cache aggressively without becoming stale forever.
4. Schema references should be immutable-by-version; mutable aliases like `latest` can exist only as convenience links.
5. Registry/type lookups need cycle detection for type inheritance, schema references, and relationship expansion.
6. Generic clients need a maximum rendered field count and progressive disclosure for very wide objects.
7. Large collections must never be embedded by default in parent resources; use links/cursors to prevent accidental megabyte envelopes.
8. Binary/media values must use typed references rather than base64 blobs inside generic envelopes except for deliberately tiny inline representations.
9. URL/link fields need canonical relation names and safe same-origin/external distinction for UI presentation.
10. Action invocation needs CSRF/auth/session behavior inherited from existing server security architecture, not a new parallel auth scheme.
11. Field permission metadata needs three states—visible/editable/hidden or omitted—not boolean ambiguity.
12. Server must never disclose hidden field names through generic schema metadata to unauthorized clients when those names are themselves sensitive.
13. Query definitions require stable serialization so saved views, cache keys, sharing links, and tests compare meaningfully.
14. Saved views need schema/type compatibility checks when resource types evolve.
15. Pagination needs cursor-first support, while page-number metadata may be adapted only for domains that genuinely support it.
16. Event streams need resumable cursor IDs and snapshot recovery; the UI must tolerate missed events without corrupting state.
17. Job progress percentages must be optional because many operations only know stages, not honest numeric completion.
18. Cancellation needs explicit states like requested versus actually cancelled so UI never lies that work stopped immediately.
19. Retry capability must indicate whether the original inputs are preserved and whether repeated execution can duplicate effects.
20. Transform pipelines need bounded fan-out and output budgets to prevent one arbitrary input from generating unbounded resource explosions.
21. Template generation needs version pinning so regeneration later can reproduce the intended template rather than silently using the newest one.
22. Generic renderer plugins need security boundaries: only trusted local modules register executable renderers; API data selects identifiers, never code locations.
23. Renderer registry needs telemetry/diagnostics explaining why a renderer won, useful for the Resource Inspector and debugging.
24. Generic edit forms need dirty-state, navigation blocking where warranted, save-state, conflict handling, server-validation mapping, and mobile keyboard resilience.
25. Universal tables need semantic column-priority metadata but must preserve accessible table structure even when mobile presentation changes.
26. Dialog/sheet primitives need nested-overlay policy so focus trapping and z-index do not collapse under complex editors.
27. Stable UI tokens need contrast tests and system font fallbacks; visual polish cannot depend on a single remote font loading successfully.
28. RTL must be tested with mixed LTR code/URLs/numbers, not only whole-page `direction: rtl` screenshots.
29. Audit tooling needs explicit findings for raw default list markers in navigation, unscoped overflowing pre/code blocks, missing dialog labels, tiny controls, and root horizontal overflow.
30. Production rollout needs feature/capability gating so Portal generic UI can coexist with legacy pages until each integration passes runtime and compatibility tests.

## Final Revelation

The Portal should not replace every domain. It should become the interoperability language between domains and the fallback manifestation language for the UI. Specialist applications remain sovereign over their deep experiences; the Portal guarantees identity, discoverability, contracts, safety, and a dignified default rendering path.

## NEXT_ACTION

Write the final execution architecture and exact discovery checklist, then inspect the real router, entity/schema patterns, resource clients, shared shell, and style foundation before approving source files.
